Subject: Proposal: reservation lanes & ramp options for BlueForest

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached is a concise proposal (BF-Dedicated-Proposal-v1.pdf) with three reservation lanes tailored to the workload profile you shared: short pilot, anchor lane, and full reserved. High level —

1) Pilot lane (30d pilot)
   - Minimum baseline: 20 GPUs (mixed A100/80GB or equivalent)
   - Burst: up to +40 GPUs from shared pool for burst windows
   - Activation: 7-day warmup; 1-week canary
   - Use case: validation + initial inference traffic (low-latency slices)

2) Anchor lane (recommended for Q4)
   - Minimum baseline: 50 GPUs dedicated
   - Ramp schedule: 50 -> 100 over 8 weeks (triggered by sustained throughput targets)
   - Warm-start credits and prewarm + prefix cache enabled
   - SLA: 99.9% availability, dedicated support channel

3) Full reserved (scale-fast)
   - Minimum baseline: 150 GPUs dedicated
   - Staged ramp over 12 weeks with quarterly review
   - Includes priority regional capacity and warm standby lanes

Estimated per-month token/compute unit ranges and rough cost bands are in the attachment (page 2). Key implementation notes: we recommend the Anchor lane for BlueForest given your projected Q4 growth and need for predictable throughput. If you want, we can convert the pilot into a refundable credit toward the Anchor within 30 days.

Next steps: can you confirm which lane you want us to price formally for procurement (Pilot / Anchor / Full)? I can loop in Ava for a technical sizing workbook and Grace to align onboarding cadence.

Thanks,
Sergio

Dana —

Thanks — answers inline below and I’ve looped in Ava (Solutions) and Grace (Customer Success) to confirm operational details.

- Anchor minimum during week 1-2: Anchor provides a hard baseline of 50 GPUs. During the ramp we keep the baseline at 50 guaranteed; autoscaling for burst is available but will not lower the dedicated baseline. That means you have guaranteed capacity for your steady-state inference and a controlled ramp to 100. For latency preservation we recommend setting the autoscale floor at 80% of the baseline and enabling prefix/KV cache warmup during the 7-day prewarm window.

- Regional placement: We will allocate the Anchor lane in the US-West (SFO) cluster. We can provision cross-region failover to US-East for DR if you'd like.

- SLA credits: We can include a 30-day ramp credit clause in the SOW: if we miss agreed throughput/latency targets attributable to Redwood’s capacity provisioning, we will apply service credits up to 10% of the first-month license fee. Details to be finalized in procurement/legal.

Ava — can you attach the capacity workbook with a recommended GPU mix and a week-by-week ramp worksheet? Grace — what's a reasonable onboarding cadence if BlueForest picks Anchor (50->100 over 8 weeks)?

Sergio

Hi Dana —

Attached is a lightweight workbook (bf_capacity_workbook.xlsx) with our recommended sizing matrix and kernel recommendations based on the models you described (mix of 13B encoder-decoder and 70B decoder workloads). Quick highlights:

- Recommended Anchor GPU mix: 60% A100 80GB (on the baseline for KV-heavy workloads), 40% H100 where mixed precision is helpful for throughput. That maps to ~50 physical GPUs for baseline with room to convert to 1.5x logical capacity via quantization-friendly profiling.
- Week-by-week ramp (8 weeks):
   Week 0 (prewarm): enable KV cache, run synthetic load to populate caches; 7 days
   Week 1-2: baseline = 50 GPUs (dedicated) -> internal canary traffic 10% of production
   Week 3-4: ramp to 70 GPUs as traffic stabilizes; expand canary to 25%
   Week 5-8: reach 100 GPUs; full production traffic and throughput validation
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs listed in the SOW will be 50 GPUs for Anchor; autoscale burst up to 100+ (policy-driven).
- Suggested safety-net: staggered activation windows and a 1-week warm-standby lane (20 GPUs) reserved in the same region to absorb sudden spikes during the first 30 days.

Operational items for procurement/legal: power-on date, acceptance criteria (latency <= 250ms P95 for key endpoints), and credit triggers. I included a separate cost tab with an illustrative monthly delta between Anchor and Full reserved.

If useful, I can export the workbook to a one-page capacity appendix for your SOW.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
